Markdown Reader & Editor
Standalone 1.0.0 · one self-contained file · works offline · your notes stay with you

Keyboard shortcuts

  • ⌘/Ctrl+F Find in document
  • ⌘/Ctrl+E Toggle edit mode
  • ⌘/Ctrl+S Save
  • ⌘/Ctrl+Shift+A Annotate selection (keyboard)
  • ⌘/Ctrl+Z Undo last annotation
  • Ctrl+Tab Next tab · ⌘/Ctrl+W Close tab

Files & tabs

  • Open file in the sidebar, or drag & drop a .md / .markdown / .txt anywhere on the window. Open several at once - they become tabs, and reopen where you left off.

Reading & navigation

  • The sidebar outline jumps to sections. Each heading has a fold control (hover, click the chevron) to collapse its section, plus Collapse all / Expand all at the top of Contents.
  • Find (the search icon or ⌘F) highlights matches. The bottom bar shows word count (click it to switch to characters, with or without spaces) and ~reading time. Your scroll position is remembered per file, and stays put when you switch to Edit.
  • Use Aa for system, day, night or high-contrast themes, text size, justification and hyphenation. A reading-progress bar sits just under the tabs.
  • Code blocks and tables have named Copy actions. Document tabs, Notes tabs, menus, dialogs, annotations and the Notes resizer all support keyboard operation.

Highlight, colour & notes

  • Select any text to raise the pop-up toolbar: pick a highlight colour, a text colour, add a Note, or Clear what is already there. (Keyboard: select, then ⌘/Ctrl+Shift+A.)
  • A note is either a comment (a remark) or a task (a note with a checkbox you can tick off). Switch a note between the two anytime with Make task / Make comment.
  • To remove a comment: Resolve it, then Delete. A task can be deleted directly. Copy a single note, or all of them (the copy icon in the panel header), as AI-ready markdown.
  • Open the Notes panel from the top bar; the Comments | Tasks toggle filters which you see, each with a live count. Everything is saved automatically and can travel inside the .md.
  • Attached notes use quote, surrounding text, section and position anchors. If nearby wording moves or changes slightly, the reader attempts a conservative re-attachment; uncertain notes are clearly marked for manual re-attachment.

Edit, save & share

  • Edit (⌘E) the raw markdown and Save (⌘S) it back to the file. Highlights & notes can travel embedded in the .md, or exported as a separate .json.
  • Wiki-links [[Heading]] jump to headings or other open tabs; backlinks list what links here; plus footnotes and PDF export.
  • Math write $…$ for an inline formula or $$…$$ for a display one (rendered with KaTeX, fully offline).

About citations

Markdown pasted from ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity often carries leftover citation markers. We detect them and show a small ※ so you know a source was cited - but the actual link lives inside the AI chat and isn’t saved in the file, so we can’t open it. Click a marker to see the kind of source it was; use the status-bar chip to hide the markers, or Export ▸ Download .md (without citations) for a clean copy.

Private, accessible and agent-friendly

  • A strict security policy disables network connections. Remote and relative document images are replaced with their alt text and address; external links open only after your action.
  • Markdown and imported annotation data are sanitised before use. No account, analytics, CDN or package installation is required.
  • Semantic landmarks, stable heading links, named controls, live status messages and predictable keyboard patterns make the same interface usable by assistive technology and browser agents.
  • Notes copy as structured Markdown with their attached quotation, making a complete review round easy to hand to a human or AI agent.

Desktop app coming soon

The desktop app builds on this private review workflow with native file handling, local-image resolution, Mermaid diagrams, expanded code and syntax tooling, richer exports and other desktop integrations. The standalone reader intentionally remains one portable HTML file.

No automatic network requests: nothing in an opened document is fetched, and every file is sanitised before it is shown.
